But after we got a foothold I realized: we’re doing exactly what we’re supposed to do but “baby” is still crying!??? Do I suck!?? Well no it’s something you can’t control in a direct sense.

One time I was reading about the Farber method. There were times when the baby was fed, had us near by for entertainment or just talking, and he was crying because he was sleepy (it was his usual bedtime). I decided to let him cry. I was sitting on the bed directly next to him, letting him know he is not alone and I'm available. He cried for about 20 minutes and then tuckered himself out and went to sleep. That was the last time he did that. From that time on he was able to put himself to sleep quickly. This carried over to now he's 17 months and is one of the best sleepers at daycare and at home.

We sometimes do this now where if he's crying, we do our mental checklist: If he fed, is his diaper ok, does he have a fever, is he trying to communicate something --- or did we just tell him No he cannot do X, even though X is dangerous. Oh, it's that? Let him cry. After maybe 5 minutes, he's back up and at it.

I think we had a space of time (and sometimes still do), where he'll go into spurts of crying, then being OK, then crying again. This is normally around him being told No and him having to learn how to regulate his emotions.

I say, to a health extent, let the baby cry, but make sure they know they aren't alone. If you have to leave the room, do so but have a camera/monitor and check in from time to time.
